reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every finite-dimensional real inner-product normed vector space E with its Borel measurable structure and canonical volume (dimension zero is allowed), every V:E->R, every alpha,beta in the nonnegative reals, and every eta in R, assume alpha>0, alpha<=beta, V is C^2, eta>0, beta*eta<=1, and for all x,v in E, alpha*||v||^2 <= D^2 V(x)[v,v] <= beta*||v||^2. The Hessian is precisely the iterated Frechet derivative evaluated twice at v. There are no extra kernel, operator, invariance, spectral, or regularity inputs.

Set mu=vol_E.tilted(-V), namely normalized exponential tilting with weight exp(-V(x)). Let J be the pushforward of mu tensor gamma_E under (x,z)->(x,x+sqrt(eta) z), with gamma_E the standard Gaussian on E. Put nu=J.snd. Write H=L^2(nu;R) and K=L^2(J;R), spaces of almost-everywhere equivalence classes of measurable square-integrable real functions, with their real Hilbert norms and inner products. Finite dimension of E does not make H or K finite-dimensional.

For every E,V,alpha,beta,eta satisfying the stated assumptions, define mu,J,nu and H as above. There exists a bounded continuous real linear selfadjoint operator T:H->H such that, for every u in H, Tu(y)=integral u(x) rho_y(dx) for nu-almost every y, where rho_y is canonical volume normalized by the exponential weight exp(-V((y+x)/2)-||y-x||^2/(8 eta)). This is a produced operator with the stated integral action; no such operator is supplied as an assumption.

There exists q in H equal to the constant 1 nu-almost everywhere such that <q,u>=integral u dnu for every u in H. Set H0=ker(u-><q,u>), the entire closed real Hilbert subspace orthogonal to q. The pairing identity makes H0 exactly the mean-zero subspace, with the norm and inner product inherited from H. There exists a bounded continuous real linear endomorphism T0:H0->H0 such that T0u, viewed as an element of H, equals Tu for every u in H0. T0 is selfadjoint. Thus invariance of this full centered subspace and an actual restriction of T are conclusions.

Define r=alpha*eta, c=(1-r)/(1+r), b=4r/(1+r)^2, and A0=I_H0-T0 composed with T0. A0 is positive. For every u in H0, ||T0u||<=c||u||, <A0u,u>=||u||^2-||T0u||^2, and b||u||^2<=<A0u,u>. The constants have exactly these normalizations. The assumptions imply 0<r<=1, so 0<=c<1, 0<b<=1, and b=1-c^2. The endpoint r=1 is included: then c=0 and b=1, so the displayed bound forces T0=0 and A0=I_H0, also when H0 is the zero space.

Finally A0 is a unit in the algebra of bounded continuous real linear endomorphisms of H0. Concretely there exists a bounded continuous real linear B:H0->H0 with B composed with A0=I_H0 and A0 composed with B=I_H0. Invertibility is for this exact entire closed centered subspace, and operator multiplication is composition. The identity here is I_H0. This is the squared defect I_H0-T0^2, not a selected positive square root. The proposition does not assert an inverse on H, construct a square root, give a trajectory or algorithm, or state an expected query/work bound. It also does not separately assert the probability, conditional joint, full-domain contraction, or constant-fixed-point conjunctions appearing in any other packet.
